spawn_spec.prompt:
Independently perform a read-only visual fidelity and interaction QA review of the Orca Lite preview. Do not edit files. Deliverable: PASS, REVISE, or FAIL; all findings must cite screenshot region or source file and be tagged [product] or [evidence]. Stop when all three fresh states and UI sources are inspected.

User-facing intent: a dark terminal workspace UI, with stable tabs/agents/worktree navigation and a split-button lifecycle that visibly cycles none -> horizontal (two side-by-side terminal panes) -> vertical (two stacked panes) -> none (one pane), without errors.

Fresh screenshots:
- /tmp/orca-lite-final-split-horizontal.png
- /tmp/orca-lite-final-split-vertical.png
- /tmp/orca-lite-final-unsplit.png
All are 1280x720 captures from the same active preview.

Read these sources as needed: ui/src/App.tsx, ui/src/components/TerminalSplitView.tsx, ui/src/components/TerminalPane.tsx, ui/src/components/WorkspaceHeader.tsx, ui/src/components/TabBar.tsx, ui/src/components/Sidebar.tsx, ui/src/state/workspaceStore.ts, ui/src/state/layout.ts.

Manual behavioral evidence: agent-browser clicked the real accessible split control through all three states; final live snapshot named it 'Split terminal (none)' and exposed one 'Terminal input'; browser error output was empty. There is no external reference mock, so judge against the stated interaction and visual usability rather than pixel identity.

Focus on exact pane arrangement in each capture, overflow/clipping, divider/header/tab alignment, contrast/readability, affordance, visible state consistency, and whether the component tree implements the interactions rather than faking a screenshot.

</Category_Context>

final_response:
Verdict: **REVISE**.

The interaction layer is genuinely correct; the styling layer is objectively broken — the entire design-token system resolves to nothing in the shipped CSS.

## What passes

**[evidence] The split cycle is real, not a faked screenshot.** `App.tsx:handleSplit` implements `none -> horizontal -> vertical -> none` exactly as specified, `layoutReducer` ROTATE_SPLIT/DISABLE_SPLIT back it, and `TerminalSplitView` renders a real second `TerminalPane` with its own session, keyed by tab id. Pixel-verified per state:
- horizontal: a single full-height divider at x=734, two side-by-side panes each with an independent xterm buffer, prompt, and cursor.
- vertical: divider row at y=390 spanning the full content width, two stacked panes.
- unsplit: zero dividers in the content area (column-change scan at y=400 returned empty), one pane.

This matches the live a11y snapshot (`Split terminal (none)`, one `Terminal input`, empty error output). Both panes render distinct terminal instances, so the secondary pane is a real session, not a duplicated bitmap.

**[product] Navigation chrome is stable across all three captures.** Tabs (`main`, `main (2)`, `main (3)`), the three agent cards, and the worktree card are pixel-identical in all three states — switching split mode doesn't disturb surrounding structure. Active tab shows both a lighter fill and a bottom indicator bar (`TabBar.tsx`), which is unambiguous.

**[product] Terminal readability is good.** `TERMINAL_THEME` in `TerminalPane.tsx` is applied via xterm's own JS theme (not Tailwind), so it survives the CSS failure: `#d4d4d4` on `#0a0a0a` is ~13:1 contrast, and the green/gray banner colors read cleanly.

## What must be fixed

**[evidence] BLOCKER — every design token is absent from the shipped CSS.** `tailwind.config.js` defines only `background` and `foreground`, but the components use ~90 token classes. Verified against the built bundle `ui/dist/assets/index-Cfx2PEwT.css` (14,009 bytes) — all of these are literally not present:

`border-border`, `bg-card`, `bg-terminal`, `bg-sidebar`, `bg-accent`, `bg-muted`, `text-muted-foreground`, `bg-worktree-sidebar`, `bg-primary`, `text-destructive`, `border-input`, plus the sizing tokens `w-sidebar`, `h-titlebar`, `h-tabbar`, `min-w-tab`, `max-w-tab`, `max-w-error`, `max-w-agent`, and the custom utilities `drag-region`, `no-drag`, `animate-enter`, `scrollbar-sleek`, `scrollbar-none`, `terminal-host`.

There is no `@theme` block, no CSS variables — `src/index.css` is 15 lines of preflight plus a body rule. The components are written against a token system that was never defined.

**[product] Direct visual consequence: the split dividers are near-white.** I sampled the divider at x=734 (horizontal) and y=390 (vertical) as RGB(229,231,235). That is exactly Tailwind preflight's `border-color:#e5e7eb` default — `border-l`/`border-t` produce a 1px width, but `border-border` contributes no color, so the border falls back to a light-mode gray. On a `#0a0a0a` terminal this is a glaring white line, the single highest-contrast element on screen. In a dark terminal workspace the divider should be the *quietest* separator; here it out-shouts the active-tab indicator and every text label. Same defect hits the header border, tab-bar border, and sidebar borders.

**[product] Panel backgrounds are collapsing into one another.** `bg-card`, `bg-sidebar`, `bg-worktree-sidebar`, and `bg-terminal` all resolve to nothing, so the sidebar, tab bar, and terminal area are separated only by those white hairlines rather than by intended tonal steps. The sidebar/main boundary at x≈188 is a bare color step from (9,9,11) to (10,10,10) — a 1-value difference, effectively invisible. The panel hierarchy the design implies is not being communicated.

**[product] `text-muted-foreground` (25 usages) is undefined, so secondary text inherits `#fafafa`.** Labels intended as de-emphasized — "Working" status text, the `main` branch subtitles, "Local runtime", the agent task line — render at or near full-brightness white. Compare the agent cards: agent name and its status label are nearly the same weight, flattening the intended primary/secondary reading order.

**[product] Layout dimensions are surviving on accident, not intent.** `w-sidebar`, `h-titlebar`, `h-tabbar`, `min-w-tab`/`max-w-tab` don't exist, so the sidebar width (~188px), header height (60px), and tab widths are all falling out of content-driven intrinsic sizing. It happens to look reasonable at 1280x720, but nothing pins it — a longer worktree name or branch will reflow the sidebar and tab bar unpredictably. Note the tab strip already stops at x≈487 with dead space to the `+` button at x≈1262, which is the intrinsic-sizing fallback rather than a designed tab width.

**[evidence] Minor, worth noting: pane bottoms differ by 6px between states.** Terminal background extends to y=708 in horizontal and unsplit, but y=714 in vertical. This is xterm's row-quantized fit — the vertical split's shorter panes land on a different integer row boundary, leaving a variable-height gap under the panes. Not a correctness bug, but with `bg-terminal` undefined the gap shows the `#09090b` body instead of matching the terminal, making it read as a seam.

**[product] The split control gives no persistent visual state.** `WorkspaceHeader.tsx` swaps the icon (`SplitSquareHorizontal`/`SplitSquareVertical`) and applies `bg-accent` when split is active — but `bg-accent` is undefined, so the active-state highlight never renders. In the captures the button at x≈1234 looks identical between the horizontal and vertical states apart from a subtle glyph change. The `aria-label` correctly reports state, so screen-reader users get what sighted users don't.

## Recommendation

The component tree, state machine, and interaction wiring are sound — I'd ship this logic as-is. Blocking issue is entirely in the styling layer: define the token set (colors, the `titlebar`/`tabbar`/`sidebar`/`tab` sizing values, and the custom utilities) in `tailwind.config.js` and `index.css`, then rebuild. Until then the dark-workspace intent is not met, most visibly via the white dividers.

I made no edits; `git status` shows only pre-existing modifications from prior work.
